26-qf2-bm-2117.solution: Let x litres be the 50% solution, so 1 − x litres is the 10% solution. The pure content gives 0.5x + 0.1(1 − x) = 0.3, so 0.4x = 0.2 and x = 0.5 L. The volume needed is 0.5 L = 500 mL.
26-qf2-bm-2117.trick: 30% is exactly halfway between 10% and 50%, so the two solutions are used in equal amounts. Half of 1 L is 500 mL.

26-qf2-bm-2123.solution: dR/dx = 50 − 4x, which is zero when x = 50 ÷ 4 = 12.5. Since d²R/dx² = −4 is negative, this is a maximum. Revenue is greatest at 12.5 units.
26-qf2-bm-2123.trick: The zeros of x(50 − 2x) are x = 0 and x = 25, and the peak is halfway between them: 12.5.

26-qf2-bm-2126.solution: Sugar to flour is 2:8, so flour = sugar × 8 ÷ 2. That is 12 × 8 ÷ 2 = 96 ÷ 2 = 48. The recipe needs 48 cups of flour.
26-qf2-bm-2126.trick: 2:8 is the same as 1:4, so multiply 12 by 4 to get 48.

26-qf2-bm-2133.solution: The longest rod is the space diagonal of the box: d = √(l² + w² + h²) = √(12² + 9² + 8²) = √(144 + 81 + 64) = √289 = 17. The rod is 17 cm long.
26-qf2-bm-2133.trick: Chain two Pythagorean triples. 12 and 9 give 15 (the 3, 4, 5 triple times 3), then 15 and 8 give 17 (the 8, 15, 17 triple).

26-qf2-bm-2136.solution: One rotation covers the circumference, C = πd = π × 40 = 40π m. Six rotations cover 6 × 40π = 240π m.
26-qf2-bm-2136.trick: Just do 40 × 6 = 240 and keep the π.

26-qf2-bm-2143.solution: The homozygous recessive frequency is q² = 0.49, so q = √0.49 = 0.7. The two allele frequencies add up to 1, so the dominant allele frequency is p = 1 − 0.7 = 0.3.
26-qf2-bm-2143.trick: √0.49 = 0.7 is the recessive allele, so take it from 1 to get 0.3.

26-qf2-bm-2150.solution: Speed is the magnitude of the velocity, |v| = √(10² + 5²) = √(100 + 25) = √125. Since 125 = 25 × 5, √125 = 5√5, which is about 11.2. The speed is 5√5 knots.
26-qf2-bm-2150.trick: Take out the common factor 5: v = 5(2i + j), so the speed is 5√(4 + 1) = 5√5.

26-qf2-bm-2155.solution: Total magnification is the eyepiece power times the objective power. That is 15 × 10 = 150, so the total magnification is 150x.
26-qf2-bm-2155.trick: 15 × 10 is just 15 with a zero added: 150.

26-qf2-bm-2158.solution: Perpendicular lines have slopes that are negative reciprocals, so m₂ = −1/m₁. That makes m₁ × m₂ = −1, as with slopes 2 and −1/2. The product is −1.
26-qf2-bm-2158.trick: Remember negative reciprocals: slopes 2 and −1/2 multiply to −1.

26-qf2-bm-2165.solution: Write the system as AX = B with A = [[2, 1], [1, −1]], X = (x, y) and B = (5, 1). The determinant is 2(−1) − 1(1) = −3, so A⁻¹ = (1/3)[[1, 1], [1, −2]]. Then X = A⁻¹B = (1/3)(6, 3) = (2, 1). So x = 2 and y = 1.
26-qf2-bm-2165.trick: Add the two equations to cancel y: 3x = 6, so x = 2, then y = 2 − 1 = 1. Only the third option has x = 2.

26-qf2-bm-2204.solution: The standard normal Z has mean 0 and standard deviation 1 by definition. Its variance is therefore 1² = 1. The option σ² is just the general symbol for variance. For Z its value is 1, so the answer to give is 1.
26-qf2-bm-2204.trick: Standard normal means mean 0 and variance 1, so pick 1. Zero is the mean, not the variance.

26-qf2-bm-2210.solution: The number accepted is 25% of 8,500, which is 8,500 ÷ 4 = 2,125 students.
26-qf2-bm-2210.trick: 25% is a quarter. Half of 8,500 is 4,250, and half of that is 2,125.

26-qf2-bm-2216.solution: The 10th percentile means 10% of the scores are at or below 22. So the share above 22 is 100% − 10% = 90%. None of the three printed options shows 90%, but 90% is the correct answer.
26-qf2-bm-2216.trick: Subtract from 100: 100 − 10 = 90. The 10th percentile leaves 90% above it.
26-qf2-bm-2216.comment: Agrees with the worked out 90%. None of the three options (80%, 60%, 40%) equals 90%, so the options need fixing. The show's 80% would fit a 20th percentile, not the 10th.

26-qf2-bm-2222.solution: Because the events are independent, P(both) = 0.3 × 0.4 = 0.12. Then P(at least one) = 0.3 + 0.4 − 0.12 = 0.58. So the probability is 58%.
26-qf2-bm-2222.trick: It must be above 40% (the larger single chance) and below 70% (the plain sum counts the overlap twice), so only 58% fits.

26-qf2-bm-2230.solution: For a geometric distribution counting trials up to and including the first success, the expected number of trials is 1/p. With p = 0.2, that is 1 ÷ 0.2 = 5 trials.
26-qf2-bm-2230.trick: 0.2 is one fifth, so flip it: the expected number of trials is 5.

26-qf2-bm-2239.solution: PENALTY has 7 different letters. T takes the first place and E takes the middle (fourth) place, which leaves 5 letters for the other 5 places. They can be arranged in 5! = 5 × 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 120 ways.
26-qf2-bm-2239.trick: Two letters are locked in, so only the other 5 move: 5! = 120.

26-qf2-bm-2247.solution: A line chart joins points in time order, so it shows whether values rise, fall or stay steady over time. A scatter plot shows the link between two variables, and a bar chart compares categories. So the best choice for trends over time is the line chart.
26-qf2-bm-2247.trick: The words 'trends' and 'over time' point straight to a line chart.

26-qf2-bm-2252.solution: Simple interest is I = PRT ÷ 100, with P = ₦8,000, R = 9 and T = 4. So I = 8,000 × 9 × 4 ÷ 100 = 80 × 36 = ₦2,880.

26-qf2-bm-2259.solution: Order does not matter, so use combinations: C(9, 4) = 9! ÷ (4! × 5!) = (9 × 8 × 7 × 6) ÷ (4 × 3 × 2 × 1) = 3,024 ÷ 24 = 126 ways.
26-qf2-bm-2259.trick: Cancel before multiplying: 8 ÷ (4 × 2) = 1 and 6 ÷ 3 = 2, which leaves 9 × 7 × 2 = 126.

26-qf2-bm-2262.solution: The seven daily ranges are 20, 25, 18, 22, 30, 15 and 24. The range of these is the largest minus the smallest: 30 − 15 = 15. So the answer is 15 °F.
26-qf2-bm-2262.trick: Spot the biggest (30) and the smallest (15) and subtract: 15.

26-qf2-bm-2272.solution: A 25% increase means multiplying by 1.25. So the required GPA is 3.5 × 1.25 = 3.5 + 0.875 = 4.375.

26-qf2-bm-2279.solution: Reading p² as the squared distance from the origin, p² = X² + Y². For a value uniform on (0, L), the mean of its square is L²/3. X runs over (0, 1) and Y over (0, 2), so E[X²] = 1/3 and E[Y²] = 4/3. Then E[p²] = 1/3 + 4/3 = 5/3.
26-qf2-bm-2279.trick: For a value uniform on (0, L), the mean square is L²/3. So it is 1/3 + 4/3 = 5/3.
26-qf2-bm-2279.computed: 5/3 (reading p² as the squared distance from the origin)
26-qf2-bm-2279.comment: The question never says what p is. Reading p² as the squared distance from the origin, X² + Y², gives 5/3, which is the show's answer. Other readings give other values, for example E[(X + Y)²] = 8/3.

26-qf2-bm-2283.solution: Expected values add, so the expected total is 40 × 5 = 200 presentations.

26-qf2-bm-2291.solution: Order matters, because first and second place are different. There are 10 choices for first place and then 9 runners left for second, so 10 × 9 = 90 ways.
